## 1. Introduction

Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is the most common form of cardiovascular 
disease and the leading cause of death globally, responsible for 17.9 million 
deaths annually (WHO, 2023). CAD occurs when the coronary arteries that supply 
blood to the heart become narrowed or blocked due to plaque buildup. Early 
identification of high-risk patients using routine clinical measurements can 
assist clinicians in making faster diagnostic decisions, potentially saving lives.

This project applies bioinformatics methods to classify patients as having 
Coronary Artery Disease or not, using clinical data from the Cleveland Heart 
Disease Dataset.

## 2. Data

The Cleveland Heart Disease Dataset was collected in 1988 at the Cleveland 
Clinic Foundation and published by Detrano et al. (1989) in the American 
Journal of Cardiology. It is publicly available from the UCI Machine Learning 
Repository. The dataset contains 303 patients and 14 clinical variables used 
to predict the presence of Coronary Artery Disease (CAD).

## 3. Data Import and Cleaning

```{r load-libraries}
# Load all required packages
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)
library(e1071)
library(pheatmap)
library(pROC)
library(randomForest)
```

```{r import-data}
# Load the dataset
df <- read.csv("C:/Users/ADMIN/Documents/Bioinformatic-Project---2020-ASP-83/Data/heart.csv")

# Check size
dim(df)

# Check for missing values
sum(is.na(df))

# Convert categorical variables to factors
df$sex <- factor(df$sex, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Female", "Male"))
df$cp <- factor(df$cp, levels = c(0,1,2,3), labels = c("Typical Angina", "Atypical Angina", "Non-anginal", "Asymptomatic"))
df$fbs <- factor(df$fbs, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
df$restecg <- factor(df$restecg, levels = c(0,1,2), labels = c("Normal", "Abnormal", "Hypertrophy"))
df$exang <- factor(df$exang, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
df$target <- factor(df$target, levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No Disease", "Heart Disease"))

# Check cleaned data
str(df)
```

## 5. Statistical Tests

```{r stats-tests}
# T-tests for continuous variables
t_age <- t.test(age ~ target, data = df)
t_chol <- t.test(chol ~ target, data = df)
t_thalach <- t.test(thalach ~ target, data = df)
t_trestbps <- t.test(trestbps ~ target, data = df)

cat("=== T-TEST RESULTS ===\n")
cat("\nAge p-value:", round(t_age$p.value, 4))
cat("\nCholesterol p-value:", round(t_chol$p.value, 4))
cat("\nMax Heart Rate p-value:", round(t_thalach$p.value, 4))
cat("\nBlood Pressure p-value:", round(t_trestbps$p.value, 4))

# Chi-squared tests
chi_sex <- chisq.test(table(df$sex, df$target))
chi_cp <- chisq.test(table(df$cp, df$target))
chi_exang <- chisq.test(table(df$exang, df$target))

cat("\n\n=== CHI-SQUARED TEST RESULTS ===\n")
cat("\nSex p-value:", round(chi_sex$p.value, 6))
cat("\nChest Pain p-value:", round(chi_cp$p.value, 6))
cat("\nExercise Angina p-value:", round(chi_exang$p.value, 6))
```

## 6. Bioinformatics Classification Models

```{r train-test-split}
# Fix factor levels and split data
set.seed(123)

df$target <- factor(df$target, 
                    levels = c("No Disease", "Heart Disease"),
                    labels = c("NoDisease", "HeartDisease"))

trainIndex <- createDataPartition(df$target, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- df[trainIndex, ]
test_data <- df[-trainIndex, ]

cat("Training set rows:", nrow(train_data))
cat("\nTest set rows:", nrow(test_data))
```

```{r logistic-regression}
# Logistic Regression
set.seed(123)

log_model <- train(target ~ .,
                   data = train_data,
                   method = "glm",
                   family = "binomial",
                   trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", 
                                          number = 5,
                                          classProbs = TRUE))

log_pred <- predict(log_model, test_data)
log_cm <- confusionMatrix(log_pred, test_data$target)
print(log_cm)
```

```{r random-forest}
# Random Forest
set.seed(123)

rf_model <- train(target ~ .,
                  data = train_data,
                  method = "rf",
                  trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", 
                                         number = 5,
                                         classProbs = TRUE))

rf_pred <- predict(rf_model, test_data)
rf_cm <- confusionMatrix(rf_pred, test_data$target)
print(rf_cm)
```

```{r svm-model}
# SVM model
set.seed(123)

svm_model <- svm(target ~ ., 
                 data = train_data, 
                 kernel = "radial",
                 probability = TRUE)

svm_pred <- predict(svm_model, test_data)
svm_cm <- confusionMatrix(svm_pred, test_data$target)
print(svm_cm)
```

```{r roc-curves}
# ROC curves
log_prob <- predict(log_model, test_data, type = "prob")[,2]
rf_prob <- predict(rf_model, test_data, type = "prob")[,2]
svm_prob_raw <- predict(svm_model, test_data, probability = TRUE)
svm_prob <- attr(svm_prob_raw, "probabilities")[,2]

roc_log <- roc(test_data$target, log_prob)
roc_rf <- roc(test_data$target, rf_prob)
roc_svm <- roc(test_data$target, svm_prob)

cat("Logistic Regression AUC:", round(auc(roc_log), 4))
cat("\nRandom Forest AUC:", round(auc(roc_rf), 4))
cat("\nSVM AUC:", round(auc(roc_svm), 4))

png("C:/Users/ADMIN/Documents/Bioinformatic-Project---2020-ASP-83/Output/figure5_roc_curves.png", 
    width = 1200, height = 900, res = 150)
plot(roc_log, col = "blue", lwd = 2, main = "Figure 5: ROC Curves for All Models")
plot(roc_rf, col = "red", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
plot(roc_svm, col = "green", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c(paste("Logistic Regression AUC =", round(auc(roc_log), 3)),
                  paste("Random Forest AUC =", round(auc(roc_rf), 3)),
                  paste("SVM AUC =", round(auc(roc_svm), 3))),
       col = c("blue", "red", "green"), lwd = 2)
dev.off()

plot(roc_log, col = "blue", lwd = 2, main = "Figure 5: ROC Curves for All Models")
plot(roc_rf, col = "red", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
plot(roc_svm, col = "green", lwd = 2, add = TRUE)
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c(paste("Logistic Regression AUC =", round(auc(roc_log), 3)),
                  paste("Random Forest AUC =", round(auc(roc_rf), 3)),
                  paste("SVM AUC =", round(auc(roc_svm), 3))),
       col = c("blue", "red", "green"), lwd = 2)
```

```{r feature-importance}
# Feature Importance
importance_data <- varImp(rf_model)$importance
importance_data$Feature <- rownames(importance_data)
importance_data <- importance_data[order(importance_data$Overall, decreasing = TRUE),]

plot6 <- ggplot(importance_data, aes(x = reorder(Feature, Overall), y = Overall)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#66B2FF", color = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Figure 6: Feature Importance from Random Forest",
       x = "Clinical Feature", y = "Importance Score") +
  theme_minimal()

print(plot6)
ggsave("C:/Users/ADMIN/Documents/Bioinformatic-Project---2020-ASP-83/Output/figure6_feature_importance.png", 
       plot6, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r clustering}
# K-means clustering
set.seed(123)

cluster_data <- df[, c("age", "trestbps", "chol", "thalach", "oldpeak", "ca")]
scaled_data <- scale(cluster_data)
km <- kmeans(scaled_data, centers = 2, nstart = 25)
df$cluster <- factor(km$cluster)

plot7 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = age, y = thalach, color = cluster, shape = target)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("1" = "#FF9999", "2" = "#66B2FF")) +
  labs(title = "Figure 7: K-means Clustering of Patients",
       x = "Age (years)", y = "Max Heart Rate (bpm)",
       color = "Cluster", shape = "Diagnosis") +
  theme_minimal()

print(plot7)
ggsave("C:/Users/ADMIN/Documents/Bioinformatic-Project---2020-ASP-83/Output/figure7_clustering.png", 
       plot7, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

## 7. Results and Discussion

The Random Forest bioinformatics classification model achieved the highest 
accuracy of 83.33% and AUC of 0.91, outperforming Logistic Regression 
(81.67%, AUC 0.87) and SVM (80.00%, AUC 0.86). Feature importance analysis 
revealed that maximum heart rate (thalach), number of major vessels (ca), 
and thalassemia type (thal) were the strongest predictors of Coronary Artery 
Disease (CAD). Statistical tests confirmed significant differences between 
CAD and non-CAD groups for age, max heart rate, blood pressure, sex, chest 
pain type and exercise angina (p < 0.05). Cholesterol was not statistically 
significant (p = 0.136). The k-means clustering analysis identified two 
natural patient clusters aligned with age and heart rate, consistent with 
the classification results.

## 8. Conclusion

This project successfully demonstrated that bioinformatics classification 
models can predict Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) from routine clinical 
measurements with over 80% accuracy. The Random Forest model was the best 
performer with an AUC of 0.91. Maximum heart rate and number of major vessels 
were identified as the most important diagnostic features. Future work could 
include larger and more diverse datasets, integration of genomic biomarkers, 
and deep learning approaches to further improve CAD prediction accuracy.

## 9. Reproducibility

To reproduce this analysis:
1. Clone the repository from GitHub
2. Install R packages: ggplot2, caret, e1071, pheatmap, pROC, randomForest
3. Run Data/download.R to download the dataset
4. Open Code/analysis.Rmd in RStudio and click Knit to HTML
